planting.note: Plant nursery-propagated rhizomes in fall in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in bright to full shade; this Japanese woodland species goes fully dormant by summer and resents being disturbed once established.

directions: Plant nursery-propagated rhizomes in fall in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in bright to full shade. Trillium apetalon is an uncommon Japanese woodland species notable for lacking true petals altogether, instead showing small, red-to-burgundy sepals above a whorl of mottled leaves in early spring. It is a true spring ephemeral that disappears by summer, so mark its location and avoid disturbing the root zone during dormancy.

planting.note: Plant nursery-propagated rhizomes in fall in cool, humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; this cold-hardy northern Japanese species prefers a sheltered woodland site that stays cool through summer.

directions: Plant nursery-propagated rhizomes in fall in cool, humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial to full shade. Trillium channellii is a robust tetraploid species endemic to Hokkaido in northern Japan, closely related to T. camschatcense, producing broad leaves and comparatively large, pure white pedicellate flowers in spring. Uncommon in cultivation outside specialty bulb nurseries, it is best obtained only from nurseries propagating stock rather than wild-collected plants.
